page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by 64 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 physical cores running at 2.6 GHz on the arm64 architecture. It features 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in the PassMark memory score and Geekbench multi-core tests, alongside strong memory bandwidth metrics, reaching 253.52 GB/sec for large-block read operations. Database and caching workloads perform well, with Redis SET operations reaching 101.36 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring in the strong tier. However, single-core performance is average, and text generation for small LLM models is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the poor tier.

The r7gd.16xlarge offers high resource density by combining a large memory footprint with high-capacity local NVMe storage on an energy-efficient ARM architecture. This combination provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and I/O-heavy workloads without the overhead of external storage. The instance is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.

It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a 30 Gbps baseline network speed. While single-core processing and small-model LLM text generation are average to poor, the instance excels in memory-bound and high-I/O environments.
